title: The Roaring Forties
subtitle: Summer ends here, the icy sea begins.

content.text: I have some news you'll be happy to hear.

branch.text: Trust me, you'll wish you had more than a minute for this. It involves a mutual friend of ours—a long-lost acquaintance you've been searching for.
Doctor, writer ... she goes by many titles, just like you and I. Sadly, in her current state, her brain capacity is limited.
It's just like after that fateful battle ended. Few survived to remember her awe-inspiring feats.
Now, this kind-hearted doctor has become a crucial part of another wicked scheme of which our dear admiral is well aware.
An orchestra without a conductor can barely play a symphony. Recognizing that missing, vital piece, the admiral seized the opportunity without hesitation.
Experience gives a veteran his scars, yes, but also a scrap of wisdom. He knew he should gain the upper hand in this one-sided gamble.
I don't know yet; there's no mention of it in the reports. I do have some speculations, however.
Those troublemakers have been focused on nothing but cultivating chaos and fanning the flames of conflict, paying little attention to the scale and extent of their intended retribution.

Now, it seems they've realized the uncertainty of this approach—drastic, volatile retribution won't get them anywhere. To reach their destination, they must forge a new path, even if it's more arduous and perilous than the last.
Your minute's up. Time certainly does fly, doesn't it?
I'll be back when there's a new development. Stay alive if you can. I'd like to keep reading reports for you.

trails.title: Paths of the Past - Dr. Dores

content.text: A strangely shaped typewriter; the only weapon this doctor had in her battle with fate.

items.text: The Roaring Forties
Clifftop, Tierra del Fuego
You made the right choice.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: We simply followed THEIR guidance, Preacher.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Unfortunately, we failed to bring the succubus.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: But I did bring you this, and Ms. Urd, as well.

items.speaker: Sophia the Preacher
items.text: No, Admiral. Not you ...

items.speaker: Sophia the Preacher
items.text: Us.

items.speaker: Sophia the Preacher
items.text: We all need the miracle THEY bestow.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: My men will not wear the masks. Nor will they take the trials.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: We need no trials to test the loyalty of my children, Preacher.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: And for now, Ms. Urd will stay under my protection.

items.speaker: Sophia the Preacher
items.text: As you wish.
The Preacher agrees to all of the admiral's requests.
It doesn't matter. None of it matters.
She looks southward across the sea.

items.speaker: Sophia the Preacher
items.text: Until next time, Admiral.
The Preacher takes the relic left by the Mother of Resurrection and bids farewell to the admiral.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Father.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I shot at Lopera.
Shooting is one thing. Whether the bullet hits the heart or the ground is another. To the admiral, however, it is unimportant.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I have to be honest, Father. I don't fully agree with your decision, at least not on a personal level.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: You're entitled to your opinion, Lieutenant. But I don't need your approval.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I understand. You only need my obedience.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Precisely.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Had you anticipated that Lopera wouldn't come with us?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: She is inconsequential. She helped us retrieve Urd from that Brotherhood farce. That's all I needed from her.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: But the Brotherhood ... With all due respect, admiral ...

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: I've heard they have connections with our "friends" at Manus Vindictae.
She finds it hard to call those they once fought against "friends."
Treason is a stain not easily washed clean.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I thought you'd make the same choice she did.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: No, I will always follow you, Father.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Just let her be.
A lone seagull glides across the sky, calling out as it flies to the warm north.
Igor pats his daughter on the shoulder.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Now, bring me Dr. Dores.

items.speaker: Moldir
items.text: Father.
She dutifully leads the doctor to her father and leaves the two alone.

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: I don't know you, sir. You must have mistaken me for someone else.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: No, I couldn't possibly mistake you.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Old friend.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: In the last days before the millennium, we fought side by side.
Memories flood the weathered halls of the old admiral's mind.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: In hindsight, that battle may have been a mistake.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: The "Storm" swept across the world, leaving behind an era of chaos.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: And we lost our future.
The admiral has never been fearful of sacrifice, especially when it has served the grander goal.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: But now, another path lies before us, one that we once fought desperately against.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: A path paved by Arcana.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: A path leading to a world free of conflict.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: My old friend.
Sadly, she cannot comprehend even a fragment of these words.
She's simply Doctor Dores. Nothing more.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: That marble chair the Foundation gave you ... What's the secret behind it?

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: What happened to you after you pressed that button?

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: Nothing.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Do you remember what happened after you walked into that white house?

items.speaker: Doctor Dores
items.text: I'm sorry. I don't know anything about that.
She's stubborn but answers honestly.
The old admiral sighs and pulls a stack of UTTU magazines from his coat. They were not for his own reading.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: My dear Ms. Urd.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: Your name continues to show up between the occurrences of the "Storm."

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: I don't know what you've encountered, what you've experienced, in all this time.

items.speaker: Admiral Igor
items.text: But your very existence is about to change the fate of us all.
TO BE CONTINUED…
